note: Filled in by hand. `21st init --design-context` detects nothing here: it looks for a JS framework and a token file it recognises, and this console is a Rust crate that inlines its own CSS and JS. Everything below was read out of those files or measured in a browser against the running console. `21st init --design-context --refresh` would overwrite it.

project.name: velstra-cloud-console
project.productType: operator console for an IaaS control plane

instructions: velstra-cloud-console/src/lib.rs (module doc: what the console is for)

design.colorMode: dark-first, both appearances re-pointed from one token set

colors.text: --text-strong, --text-body, --text-muted, --text-faint (four levels, every one at or above 4.5:1 on every ground it is painted on)
colors.interaction: --brand / signal blue #2e96c4 dark, #2179a1 light — links, focus, selection, active navigation, the one primary action
colors.status-text: --green-300 / --amber-300 / --red-300 — the same three at text weight, lighter on dark and darker on light
colors.product: --product, the platform's own mark; never the interaction colour

typography.families: --font-sans: system-ui stack only; --font-mono: ui-monospace stack. No webfont, ever.
typography.mono-is-for: object names, paths, identifiers, log lines, wire addresses

spacing.reading-layout: --gutter 180px + --gutter-gap 28px — labels have one left edge, content the other

radius.rule: 4px default, 6px the largest ordinary surface, pill for status dots only

shadows.rule: elevation and a 1px border say 'this is over that'; no tint, no blur

motion.easing: --ease-out, --ease-in-out, --ease-settle (critically damped: arrives and stops, no overshoot)
motion.rule: almost nothing moves; what does, moves because it carries information
motion.reduced-motion: every animation has a still equivalent that says the same thing

design.density: compact — dense tables, 13px body, 44px row pitch

preferredPrimitives: .btn / .btn.primary / .btn.quiet — the quiet one takes its colour when the pointer arrives
.btn.busy — a press that waits on the API says so; use it, do not invent a spinner
.state.<verdict> + mark() — the verdict word and its dot, the one way status is shown
.overpanel / .overrow / .linky — the overview's panel, row and way-through
.tally / .tallybtn — a count broken into parts that narrow the list under them
.tblwrap > table — every wide thing scrolls in its own container
el() in dom.js — the only element factory; there is no template language
patterns: spec vs status, and a verdict derived from generation against observed_generation in one function so no two screens disagree
board (list) → sheet (one object, modal drawer with a scrim) → form
the margin column carries the label, the content column carries the answer

must: Fetch nothing. No CDN, no webfont, no icon set, no framework: an operator opens this during an incident, sometimes from a network that reaches only the API.
Define every custom property you reference. A var() with no definition and no fallback is an invalid declaration that silently does nothing — 25 of them were found this way on 2026-09-06.
Keep both appearances resolving from one token set; never write a colour literal in a component rule.
Every text colour clears 4.5:1 on every ground it is actually painted on, measured by compositing, not read off the token table.
Colour is never the only carrier: a verdict is a word and a dot, not a hue.
Every animation has a reduced-motion equivalent that carries the same fact without moving.
avoid: Glass, blur and translucent materials: 'on a page of dense tables it costs twice'.
Radii above 6px: 'a rounded card invites you to swipe it'; infrastructure surfaces are regions of a page, not objects to pick up.
Spring and bounce: 'a panel that bounces on open is a panel an operator sees bounce forty times a day'.
Numbers that count up: a figure that animates is a figure you cannot read while it moves.
The interaction colour as a status or a progress fill: signal blue 'never means healthy, and it never fills a progress bar'.
Decorative gradients, hero headlines, icon-only controls.

decisions.what: The light ramp re-points the -300 status colours as well as the -500 ones.
decisions.why: `.state` writes every object's verdict in the -300 ramp, which light.css never re-pointed: 'not settled' read 1.47:1 and 'Settled' 1.78:1 on a white page. On a light ground 'text weight' means darker than the dot, not lighter.

decisions.what: --slate-300 added; --text-faint points at it instead of --ink-300.
decisions.why: --ink-300 as faint text read 2.99:1 on a raised card. --slate-300 clears 4.5:1 on every dark ground and stays a step under --slate-400, so the four text levels keep their order.

decisions.what: Six token names that resolve to nothing were mapped onto the real vocabulary: --text→--text-body, --text-dim→--text-muted, --mono→--font-mono, --accent→--brand, --radius→--radius-lg, --border-faint→--border-subtle.
decisions.why: 25 declarations across the overview, the map, the label filter, the log block, the CPU advisory and the VNC screen were invalid and silently did nothing — including three focus and active-state indicators.

decisions.what: The attention list is ordered by verdict, not by collection.
decisions.why: unsettledEverywhere() walked the rail in order, so a failing guest could sit below three networks that had merely not reported. Its own doc comment already claimed an order it did not produce.

decisions.what: One animation was added to the boards and no others: a row whose verdict changed on the last refresh is washed once, 900ms on --ease-settle, with a 2px edge instead under reduced motion.
decisions.why: It carries what the table cannot — which of forty rows is not what it was a moment ago. Motion that only decorates was declined; see `avoid`.

decisions.what: Rows in the attention list were left as they are: the name is the way through, the row is not a target.
decisions.why: Proposed and withdrawn after reading the code. `.linky` is already a focusable button and its comment is deliberate: 'it is a way through, not an action'. What was actually missing was its hover colour, which was one of the dead tokens.

evidence: Every text node on 33 boards and their sheets, in both appearances at 1600px and 430px, composited over its real background: 5878 findings before the light-ramp fix, 398 after, all four remaining ones measured as conforming.
Target sizes checked by hit test rather than by rectangle: the 13x13 row checkboxes have 44px between them, so WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception applies.
Computed styles on the overview before the token migration: panel border-radius 0px, ATTENTION heading at body strength, object paths in the sans stack.
